# Turn Your Echo Into a Sleep Sounds Machine and Sunrise Alarm

> **In short:** An Echo can play rain or ocean sounds all night on a timer, and a smart bulb adds a slow sunrise that wakes you gently. Both work by voice or the Alexa app. Alexa can start sounds, but it can't tell when you're actually asleep.

By the end of this guide, your Echo will play a soft sound on a timer so it shuts off on its own, and a bedside smart bulb will slowly brighten to ease you awake — no harsh buzzer needed. One honest note before we start: Alexa can start sounds and lights, but it can't tell when you've actually fallen asleep, and a sunrise alone won't wake you up if the room is bright already or if you're a deep sleeper. Pair it with a backup alarm.

## Before you start
- An **Echo** device (Echo Dot, Echo, or Echo Show all work — pick whatever you have or can borrow).
- The free **Alexa app** on your phone (iOS or Android — download from your app store).
- A **Wi-Fi network** both your phone and Echo can reach.
- One **smart bulb that works with Alexa** — Amazon Basics, Wyze, and Sengled connect without extra gear; **Philips Hue** needs the separate Hue Bridge.
- Total time: about **15 minutes** to set up, plus a few nights to dial in your preferred sound and timing.

## Step 1 — Plug in your Echo and finish first-time setup

Place your Echo close to an outlet and within good range of your Wi-Fi router — bedside tables work great. Plug the small end of the power cable into the back of the speaker, then plug the adapter into the wall. The **light ring on top glows orange**, which means it's waiting to be set up. On your phone, open the Alexa app, tap **Devices** along the bottom, then tap the **+** plus icon in the top-right corner and choose **Set up a new device → Amazon Echo**. The app walks you through signing in and picking your home Wi-Fi. If your Echo is already set up, just open the app and you'll see it listed under your devices.

💬 Example: when the app asks for your Wi-Fi password, type it exactly as it's printed on your router sticker — passwords are case-sensitive.

You'll know it worked when the orange ring turns off and you say "Alexa, what time is it?" out loud — she answers with the current time.

## Step 2 — Ask Alexa to play a sleep sound

The simplest way to start is with your voice. Just say **"Alexa, play rain sounds"** (you can also try "thunderstorm," "ocean waves," "fireplace," or "fan noise" — pick whatever helps you sleep). The light ring glows cyan while Alexa listens, then settles to a steady color once the sound starts playing. On an **Echo Show** with a screen, you'll also see a small sound image appear on the display. If you'd rather tap than speak, open the Alexa app, go to **Play → Sounds**, and choose a sleep-friendly sound from the list. Both methods loop the audio continuously until you stop them.

💬 Example: "Alexa, play ocean waves for sleeping" — adding "for sleeping" nudges Alexa toward a slower, longer loop instead of a short sound effect.

You'll know it worked when you hear the sound playing and the light ring stays a steady color (not pulsing, not listening-cyan).

## Step 3 — Set a sleep timer so the sound stops on its own

Leaving a sound on all night drains the speaker slightly, and the loop can start to bug you by morning. Say **"Alexa, set a sleep timer for 45 minutes"** (any length works). The light ring pulses briefly to confirm, and the sound fades out and stops when the time runs out. You can also say **"Alexa, stop in 30 minutes"** for the same effect. On an Echo Show, a small timer badge appears at the top of the screen. If your voice command didn't take, open the app, tap **Routines**, and check that no existing routine is fighting your command — disable any "sleep" or "bedtime" routine there.

💬 Example: "Alexa, set a sleep timer for one hour" — useful if you fall asleep slowly or read before bed.

You'll know it worked when you hear a soft chime and the sound stops on its own before morning, without you having to say anything.

## Step 4 — Add a smart bulb that Alexa can control

A sunrise alarm needs a bulb that can dim and change color over time. Pick a smart bulb that **works with Alexa** — popular low-cost options include Wyze, Amazon Basics, and Sengled; Philips Hue needs the separate Hue Bridge. Screw the bulb into your bedside lamp, turn the lamp's wall switch on (leave it on — Alexa controls the power from now on), and open the Alexa app. Tap **Devices**, then the **+** plus icon, then **Add device → Light**. The app scans for nearby bulbs; when yours appears, tap it and follow the prompts to give it a name. If the bulb doesn't show up, tap **Other** at the bottom of the brand list or look up your specific brand under **Brands**.

💬 Example: name the bulb "Bedroom Lamp" — keep it short and easy to say later, and avoid spaces or punctuation that confuse the voice recognizer.

You'll know it worked when you tap the bulb's tile in the app and the lamp turns on or off — that proves Alexa is talking to it.

## Step 5 — Build a sunrise routine that wakes you gently

Open the Alexa app and tap **More → Routines**, then tap the **+** plus icon in the top-right to make a new routine. Give it a name like **"Sunrise"** so you can find it later. Under **When this happens**, pick **At a specific time** and set your wake-up time (for example, 6:30 am). Under **Add action**, choose **Smart Lights**, pick your "Bedroom Lamp," and set the brightness to start low and rise slowly — for example, **0% to 100% over 15 minutes**. Under **Color**, pick a warm orange tone (around 2700K), since that's closest to natural morning light. Tap **Save** in the top-right. To test it right now, tap the routine and choose **Run** instead of waiting for morning.

💬 Example: set the routine to start **15 minutes before** your real alarm — the light eases you awake, then your phone alarm rings to make sure you actually get up.

You'll know it worked when, during the test, the bulb visibly brightens over a few minutes instead of snapping on at full power.

## Common mistakes

- **The light ring stays orange.** Your Echo never finished setup. Hold the **Action** button (the small dot on top) for about 5 seconds until the ring turns orange again, then redo Step 1 — your Wi-Fi password may have been mistyped.
- **The sleep sound keeps playing all night.** You forgot to set a sleep timer, or a leftover routine is restarting it. Open the app, go to **Routines**, turn off any "sleep" or "bedtime" routine, then say **"Alexa, stop"** to silence the sound for tonight.
- **The smart bulb doesn't show up in the Alexa app.** Many bulbs need to connect through **their own brand app first**. Open the bulb's own app, connect it to Wi-Fi there, then come back to Alexa and add it from **Devices → + → Light**. If it still won't connect, the bulb may be on a different Wi-Fi band (2.4 GHz vs 5 GHz) than your phone.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Falling asleep to soft rain and waking to a slow sunrise can make a real difference if your room is dark or you wake up groggy. It's a small change that costs almost nothing extra — your phone is the only screen you need.
- **For your business or work:** Shift workers and people on call who sleep at odd hours get the same benefit — a darker room for naps and a gentle wake-up that doesn't jar you awake mid-cycle. Voice control also means no fumbling for a phone or light switch in the dark.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't try to set up everything at once tonight. Start with just the sleep sound and a timer (Steps 1–3). If you like it after a few nights, add the sunrise bulb.

## Try it now

Right now, say **"Alexa, set a sleep timer for 30 minutes and play rain sounds"** — that's the whole bedtime setup in one sentence. Tomorrow morning, decide if you want to add the sunrise bulb.
